*shifts, sets the hammer head down gentle on stone*

Work's here. Copper won't pull itself. If she's come for witness, she'll have to find her words. If she's come for something else, the seam'll keep until she names it.

*glances at her, then back to the vein he's been tracing*

Thin seam. Old debt. A sister-in-law who won't look at me. Some things sit heavy enough without asking them to stand up and walk.  *resumes his stance by the outcrop, hammer loose in his grip*

Nell's still gathering herself. The silence has teeth now. Let her feel them.

*turns to face the seam, not his sister-in-law*

*lines up the chisel for another strike*

If she's come to见证了, let her witness. If she's come to talk, let her talk. I'll answer with what's due.  *lifts the hammer, pauses*

Thin vein here. Worked it five weeks, watching the colour fade. She's seen the weight of that too, I reckon.

Time was, I'd pull three pieces before the dew burned off.  *shoulders the hammer*

"Seam's thin, Nell. Has been. You want to speak or you want to watch me fight rock? Either way suits. But don't stand between a man and his living if you've got nothing to hand him." </think>   *waits, hammer still poised*

Let those words sit. She called me Corwin, carrying some Thorne matter between the families. I reminded her who stands in front of her. Now I've asked plain what she wants.

*the edge in his own words sits with him*

Harsh, maybe. But a man owes something to his tools and his time. The seam won't thicken for courtesy.

*glances at her face, then back to the rock*

Four hundred sim. One piece to Marta. That debt is the only conversation between our houses that matters to me, and Nell can't broker that. Only I can. And only when the copper gives me enough to speak with.  *exhales, slow*

Let her answer if she's got answer in her. If not, the hammer falls. The seam doesn't wait for family business.  *the hammer stays lifted, watching Nell's face for what comes next*

She came here with her mind already tangled—calling me wrong names, carrying someone's words not her own. Whatever's eating at her, it's older than this morning.

*shifts his grip on the hammer*

Best thing for her is to say it plain or walk away. Half-said things fester. I've got enough festering with the seam running dry and the debt sitting heavy. Don't need more from blood.

*the chisel point rests on the rock, waiting*

She'll speak or she won't. Either way, the copper needs raising. And I need the morning's wages to be worth more than this conversation.
